data.name: Ayshana
data.gender_notes: Ayshana is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word आयुः (āyuḥ), meaning 'life' and ईशानी (īshānī), meaning 'goddess'. Ayshana is a name of the Goddess of life, representing creation, growth, and nurturing. The name Ayshana carries the meaning “Goddess of life” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ayshana usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of life and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine femininity and creativity.
data.etymology: Ayshana belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of life.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayshana total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Ayshana, also known as Queen Ayshana, was a queen of the Chalukya Dynasty in the Deccan region of India around the 11th century. She ruled the kingdom of Kalyani, which was a center of arts, culture, and learning during this period.

Another reference to Ayshana, also known as Queen Indumati, can be found in the epic poem 'Mahabharata'. In this reference, Ayshana is described as a queen of the Vidarbha kingdom who was married to Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandava and Kaurava princes.
